name: presenter-Jay-1

name: Google-Shape-533-p58-3
text: RAM speed creates a durability gap
textPreview: RAM speed creates a durability gap

name: Google-Shape-534-p58-4
text:
The problem
RAM gives microsecond access, but a power failure erases its state. A successful-looking write can disappear after a crash.
textPreview: The problem | RAM gives microsecond access, but a power failure erases its state. A successful-looking write can disappear after a crash.

name: Content-Placeholder-3-5
text:
Our solution
Write every mutation to a durable log first. Update memory second. On restart, replay the safe log records and rebuild the cache.
textPreview: Our solution | Write every mutation to a durable log first. Update memory second. On restart, replay the safe log records and rebuild the...

name: presenter-Jay-2
text: JAY  •  SLIDE 2 OF 4

Use the ATM example: if a balance changes only in RAM, a crash loses the update. Explain that WAL combines disk durability with RAM speed.

name: Title-10-3
text: Recovery replays only safe operations

name: Content-Placeholder-8-9
text:
Standalone writes
SET and DELETE records are replayed in order to rebuild the latest state.
textPreview: Standalone writes | SET and DELETE records are replayed in order to rebuild the latest state.

name: Content-Placeholder-8-11
text:
Committed transactions
Buffered TX_SET and TX_DELETE records replay only when a COMMIT marker exists.
textPreview: Committed transactions | Buffered TX_SET and TX_DELETE records replay only when a COMMIT marker exists.

name: Content-Placeholder-8-13
text:
Incomplete transactions
A crash without COMMIT leaves no visible partial update; recovery ignores those records.
textPreview: Incomplete transactions | A crash without COMMIT leaves no visible partial update; recovery ignores those records.
